analysis: The 1024-negative trial completed successfully but failed to improve validation: macro HR@10 was 0.565 versus the stated 256-negative reference of 0.580, a decrease of 0.015. Category HR@10 was 0.610 for Movies_and_TV, 0.590 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.450 for Electronics, and 0.610 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Allocated GPU time was 284.54 seconds. Increasing sampled competitors alone did not support the hypothesized gain; these results do not establish why performance declined or whether the difference is robust. Training draws shared negatives with replacement, so 1024 draws do not guarantee 1024 unique competitors. Retain 256 negatives as the better observed reference.
code_summary: One independent MaskedSASRec model and one selected checkpoint per category, with all four dataset routes preserved. Each network uses 96-dimensional tied item embeddings, learned positional embeddings, two bidirectional pre-norm Transformer blocks with two attention heads, GELU output projection, dropout 0.2, and jointly trained item biases. Training masks the final target plus auxiliary history positions and equally weights final-mask and auxiliary-mask mean cross-entropy. The sole experimental change increased shared uniform negative draws from 256 to 1024, retaining target-collision masking. AdamW, seed 42, supplied splits, validation-based checkpoint selection, and predictor generation remained unchanged. No ensembles or independently fitted auxiliary scorers were used.
